request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due" figure (`data-testid="watched-due-total"`). It adds up the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches and shows 0.00 when they watch no one. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

This was a front-end-only change, in `src/main/frontend/features/summary/Header.tsx`. The app already loads the list of people each user watches and each person's due-total as their row shows it. The new figure adds those up the same way the "My crews due" figure does. A person whose due-total shows as n/a is skipped, so they add nothing. No stored data, server code or audit records changed, because watching was already stored and audited per user.
